Some sentences you have to read twice because your brain refuses them the first time. Here’s one.
At one of the most valuable technology companies on Earth, a large number of highly paid software engineers, people who built products used by billions, have reportedly been reassigned to generate and label training data for AI models. By hand. The same category of work that’s traditionally done by lower-wage contractors.
I sat with that for a while when the reporting first surfaced, because it inverts a story we’ve all been told. The narrative was: AI is coming for the workers, especially the routine ones. And here’s the plot twist nobody scripted: to build the AI, one of the giants turned some of its most elite workers into the routine ones. The people at the top of the food chain got handed the task at the bottom.
Let me walk through what’s been reported, why it’s happening, and what it quietly reveals about the state of AI in 2026, because the why is even more interesting than the what.
